headline_marked: [[Youth group catches criminals]] in Tongi, sparking debate over civilian policing
headline: Youth group catches criminals in Tongi, sparking debate over civilian policing
summary: A youth group in Tongi, Gazipur, is actively apprehending snatchers and drug dealers, handing them over to police. Their operations, however, raise questions about the role of civilians in law enforcement.
details: A video circulating on Facebook shows young people detaining a man identified as 'Blade Anwar' in Tongi, Gazipur. In the video, Anwar is seen warning other snatchers to stay away from Tongi, stating they would be severely beaten by "the public."
The youth group, known as "Bangladesh Youth Revolution," claims to work against snatchers, drug users, and other criminals. They apprehend suspects and hand them over to the police.

The group's central convener, Fahad Islam, stated they have 250 active members in Tongi and have received over 700 applications. Their Facebook page boasts 54,000 followers, where they regularly post videos of their operations.

Members of the "Bangladesh Youth Revolution" wear specific uniforms, patrol areas, and participate in operations, sometimes carrying sticks. They are occasionally seen alongside police personnel during their activities.

However, their actions have sparked debate, with critics questioning why civilians are performing police duties. Concerns have been raised about the risks of ordinary citizens apprehending criminals, potential harassment of innocent individuals, and the legality of publicly identifying suspects in videos.

Tongi, an area under two police stations (Tongi East and Tongi West), reportedly suffers from high crime rates, particularly snatching, despite police efforts. Local residents complain about the police's inability to curb crime effectively.

Official data from Tongi East and West police stations recorded 71 and 72 cases of snatching/attempted robbery, respectively, between June and September of the previous year. Over 1,100 suspects were arrested during this period.

Many snatching incidents go unreported or are registered as general diaries, not full cases, suggesting the official statistics may not reflect the full extent of crime. A local resident, Sheikh Mohammad Russel, shared his experience of being robbed at knifepoint in Tongi, with no recovery or arrests made in his case.

The group's founders have stated their official launch date is December 16, 2025, though they are already widely known and active in the area. They claim to have handed over approximately 250 snatchers and drug dealers to the police since their inception.

Sabuj Uddin Iqbal, a chief organizer of the group, justified their actions by stating they aim to ensure the safety of "mothers and sisters." He also claimed that some officials from the Gazipur Metropolitan Police are part of their WhatsApp group, coordinating patrols.

headline_marked: [[Bangladesh Bank launches Tk 1,000 crore loan]] for overseas workers' skill development, up to Tk 10 lakh available
headline: Bangladesh Bank launches Tk 1,000 crore loan for overseas workers' skill development, up to Tk 10 lakh available
summary: The special pre-finance scheme aims to support Bangladeshis seeking employment abroad by funding their skill development and language training. Workers can access up to Tk 10 lakh without collateral.
details: Bangladesh Bank has launched a special pre-finance scheme worth Tk 1,000 crore to assist Bangladeshis seeking overseas employment. The fund aims to enhance their skills and language proficiency for better job opportunities abroad.

Administered through Probashi Kallyan Bank, this fund allows aspiring migrant workers to take collateral-free loans of up to Tk 10 lakh. The fund will be disbursed to Probashi Kallyan Bank in five equal installments of Tk 200 crore each.
The loan carries a maximum interest rate of 9 percent. It has an initial tenure of three years, including a six-month grace period, and can be extended up to five years if needed.
While no collateral is required, applicants must provide two guarantors: one immediate family member and another socially established individual capable of repaying the loan.
The loan covers tuition fees for language or job-specific skill training, and in certain cases, accommodation and food expenses during training. However, it does not cover air ticket costs.
Eligible applicants are Bangladeshis intending to go abroad for legal employment. Students pursuing studies overseas are not eligible for this particular facility.

Applications can be submitted online via Probashi Kallyan Bank's website. After initial verification at the branch level, applications are sent to the head office for approval, with progress viewable online.
To ensure proper utilization, a two-tier monitoring system is in place. Bangladesh Bank's SME & Specials Program Division will oversee the fund's activities.
As of October 4, 2026, Tk 13.03 crore has already been disbursed to 481 individuals under this scheme, according to Probashi Kallyan Bank.
